spec_name: Learn Tracks Expansion v1 (Opening Principles, Essential Endgames, Strategic Thinking, Master Class)

context.current_ui: Learn page shows track cards with level badge, lessons count, estimated hours, progress %
context.current_db_seed: learn_tracks seeded for intermediate-openings, intermediate-endgames, advanced-strategy, expert-mastery but lessons/steps not yet created for these tracks

publishing_rules: Tracks in UI must show lesson count (published lessons only)
Estimated hours should roughly match total lesson minutes / 60 (±20%)
Lessons must have a stable slug used as route /learn/lesson/[lessonSlug]

difficulty_model.intermediate: More guided examples, fewer forced-move tasks, introduce planning concepts
difficulty_model.advanced: More calculation and decision making, longer puzzles, fewer hints
difficulty_model.expert: Model games, candidate moves, evaluation, endgame technique, reduced hints

board_content_rules: Every lesson must include at least 1 interactive element (move_task OR puzzle OR quiz)
Every track must include at least 1 practice component (puzzle steps OR a linked practice pack)
All FEN positions must be legal and consistent with required moves
Use meta.boardPrefs.orientation when black-to-move positions are used

track_outcomes: Understand opening goals: development, center, king safety
Know common opening mistakes and how to punish them
Build a simple opening repertoire framework (not memorization-heavy)
Learn how to transition into a playable middlegame

lessons.title: The 3 Goals of the Opening
lessons.description: Development, center control, king safety — and why they matter.

steps_blueprint.title: What the opening is for
steps_blueprint.body_md: Explain: get pieces out, fight for center, prepare castling.

steps_blueprint.title: Choose the best developing move
hints: Develop a knight toward the center
Prefer Nf3 over random pawn pushes

steps_blueprint.title: Common traps: ignoring king safety
steps_blueprint.body_md: Explain: early queen adventures and neglecting castling.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a main opening goal?
quiz.explainMd: Early queen moves often lose tempo and invite attacks.

lessons.title: Development: Don’t Waste Tempos
lessons.description: How to develop pieces efficiently and avoid repeated moves.

steps_blueprint.title: Tempo explained
steps_blueprint.body_md: A tempo is a move. Re-moving the same piece wastes time.

steps_blueprint.title: Punish wasted queen moves
steps_blueprint.explain_correct_md: Nc6 develops a piece and gains tempo by attacking the queen.

steps_blueprint.title: Develop with tempo
hints: Develop the bishop to an active square

quiz.question: Which move usually wastes tempo in the opening?

options.text: Moving the same piece twice without reason

quiz.explainMd: Repeated moves without purpose fall behind in development.

lessons.title: Center Control: e4/d4 & Counterplay
lessons.description: Why the center matters and how to attack/undermine it.

steps_blueprint.title: The center squares
steps_blueprint.body_md: Explain: e4, d4, e5, d5; space and mobility.

quiz.question: What is a common way to fight a strong pawn center?
quiz.explainMd: Pawn breaks challenge and dissolve the opponent’s central control.

lessons.title: King Safety: Castling & When Not To
lessons.description: Castling patterns, common attacks, and when to delay castling.

steps_blueprint.title: Why castling matters
steps_blueprint.body_md: Explain king safety + rook activation.

quiz.question: Which is usually a reason to delay castling?

options.text: You can win material immediately with a tactic

quiz.explainMd: Tactical opportunities can justify delaying castling briefly.

lessons.title: Common Opening Mistakes & Punishments
lessons.description: How to respond to early queen moves, pawn grabbing, and weak squares.

steps_blueprint.title: Mistakes to watch for
steps_blueprint.body_md: Early queen, neglect development, greedy pawn grabs.

steps_blueprint.title: Win tempo vs queen
steps_blueprint.explain_correct_md: Nc3 hits the queen and develops.

lessons.title: Build a Simple Repertoire (Principles → Plan)
lessons.description: Pick 1–2 openings and learn plans, not memorization.

steps_blueprint.title: Repertoire idea
steps_blueprint.body_md: Choose: 1.e4 or 1.d4, and a response vs each.

quiz.question: What should you learn first in an opening?
quiz.explainMd: Plans + placement create consistent, practical play.

practice_packs_required.title: Opening Principles Drills
practice_packs_required.description: Quick scenarios: develop, win tempo, castle, punish mistakes.

track_outcomes: Convert basic king+pawn endgames with opposition
Understand key rook endgame ideas (cutting off king, activity)
Know basic mating techniques (K+Q vs K, K+R vs K)
Recognize drawn vs winning pawn endings

lessons.title: King Activity & Opposition
lessons.description: The king becomes a fighting piece in the endgame.

steps_blueprint.title: King activity
steps_blueprint.body_md: Centralize king, shoulder opponent, create zugzwang.

steps_blueprint.title: Take the opposition
hints: Stand in front with one-square gap

quiz.question: Opposition usually helps you…

options.text: Win key squares and create zugzwang

quiz.explainMd: Opposition forces the opponent to give ground.

lessons.title: K+P vs K: The Key Squares
lessons.description: How to know if a pawn endgame is winning.

steps_blueprint.title: Key squares
steps_blueprint.body_md: If king reaches key squares, pawn promotes.

lessons.title: Basic Checkmates: K+Q and K+R
lessons.description: Learn the simplest mating patterns with major pieces.

steps_blueprint.title: Boxing in the king
steps_blueprint.body_md: Restrict squares step-by-step, bring king.

lessons.title: Rook Endgames: Activity & Cutting Off
lessons.description: Active rooks win. Learn cutting off the king and checking from behind.

steps_blueprint.title: Rook activity
steps_blueprint.body_md: Rooks belong behind passed pawns; keep them active.

lessons.title: Pawn Races & Outside Passed Pawn
lessons.description: Calculate pawn races and learn why outside passers win games.

steps_blueprint.title: Pawn race basics
steps_blueprint.body_md: Count tempi, opposition, and king position.

quiz.question: Why is an outside passed pawn powerful?

options.text: It deflects the king away from the center

quiz.explainMd: It drags the king away, letting you win elsewhere.

lessons.title: Endgame Checklist: What To Do First
lessons.description: A simple decision framework for practical endgames.

steps_blueprint.title: Checklist
steps_blueprint.body_md: Activate king, improve worst piece, create passer, target weaknesses.

quiz.question: In most endgames, your first priority is…
quiz.explainMd: The king becomes your strongest piece in the endgame.

practice_packs_required.title: Essential Endgames Drills
practice_packs_required.description: Opposition, key squares, rook activity, basic mates.

track_outcomes: Evaluate positions using imbalances (space, structure, piece activity)
Create plans (improve worst piece, target weaknesses, pawn breaks)
Understand pawn structures and typical plans

lessons.title: How to Evaluate a Position (Imbalances)
lessons.description: Material, king safety, structure, activity — build a clear evaluation.

steps_blueprint.title: Imbalances
steps_blueprint.body_md: List imbalances and convert them into candidate plans.

quiz.question: Which factor often matters most in quiet positions?
quiz.explainMd: Activity + structure usually define long-term advantage.

lessons.title: Pawn Structures & Typical Plans
lessons.description: Isolated pawn, doubled pawns, pawn chains, weak squares.

steps_blueprint.title: Structures
steps_blueprint.body_md: Explain: weak squares, open files, outposts.

lessons.title: Outposts & Good vs Bad Bishop
lessons.description: How to place pieces on strong squares and improve minor pieces.

steps_blueprint.title: Outpost definition
steps_blueprint.body_md: Knight supported by pawn; cannot be chased by enemy pawn.

quiz.question: What makes a square an outpost for a knight?

options.text: It is protected by a pawn and cannot be attacked by enemy pawns

quiz.explainMd: An outpost is stable and hard to challenge with pawns.

lessons.title: Prophylaxis: Stop Their Plan
lessons.description: Prevent counterplay, restrict pieces, improve safety.

steps_blueprint.title: Think like your opponent
steps_blueprint.body_md: Ask: what does opponent want? what is their best plan?

lessons.title: Converting Small Advantages
lessons.description: Trade correctly, simplify, create targets, improve worst piece.

steps_blueprint.title: Conversion rules
steps_blueprint.body_md: When ahead: trade pieces not pawns; keep king safe; improve position.

quiz.question: When you are up material, you usually want to…

options.text: Trade queens and minor pieces when safe

quiz.explainMd: Simplification reduces tactical risk and converts advantage.

lessons.title: Strategic Mini-Test (Mixed Positions)
lessons.description: A checkpoint lesson with mixed evaluation + best-plan puzzles.

quiz.question: Strategic thinking starts with…

options.text: Evaluating imbalances and making a plan

quiz.explainMd: Evaluation → plan → execution is the strategic loop.

practice_packs_required.title: Strategy Planning Drills
practice_packs_required.description: Best-plan puzzles: pawn breaks, outposts, prophylaxis, conversion.

Understand advanced endgame technique and transition decisions
Learn model games with annotated plans
Develop tournament habits: time management, practical choices

lessons.title: Candidate Moves & Calculation Tree
lessons.description: How strong players calculate: candidates, forcing moves, pruning.

steps_blueprint.title: Candidate move method
steps_blueprint.body_md: Generate candidates, prioritize forcing moves, calculate critical lines.

quiz.question: What should you calculate first?
quiz.explainMd: Forcing moves narrow the opponent’s replies and reduce branching.

lessons.title: Positional Sacrifices (When Material Doesn’t Matter)
lessons.description: Exchange sacs, initiative, domination, and practical compensation.

steps_blueprint.title: Compensation checklist
steps_blueprint.body_md: King safety, activity, structure, pawn count, piece coordination.

lessons.title: Advanced Rook Endgames (Lucena/Philidor Intro)
lessons.description: Key theoretical positions that decide real games.

steps_blueprint.title: Lucena idea
steps_blueprint.body_md: Build a bridge; cut off king; promote.

quiz.question: In rook endgames, activity usually means…

options.text: Rook behind passed pawns and checking from behind

quiz.explainMd: Active rooks create counterplay and stop pawns effectively.

lessons.title: Middlegame → Endgame Transitions
lessons.description: When to trade pieces, simplify, and choose the right endgame.

steps_blueprint.title: Trade logic
steps_blueprint.body_md: Trade into favorable pawn structure, better king, active pieces.

lessons.title: Model Game: Annotated Plan (Classic Example)
lessons.description: Replay a classic game with key moments and plans explained.

steps_blueprint.title: What to look for
steps_blueprint.body_md: Plans, pawn breaks, piece reroutes, endgame decisions.

lessons.title: Master Class Checkpoint (Mixed Test)
lessons.description: Mixed puzzles + quizzes combining calculation, strategy, and endgames.

quiz.question: Under time pressure, the best practical approach is…

options.text: Choose a solid candidate move and avoid blunders

quiz.explainMd: Practical chess rewards safe decisions and blunder-avoidance when low on time.
